title: Dihedral orbit count for binary run sequences
summary: Count binary run sequences with the maximum-length run distribution modulo the joint action of rotation and reversal.

formal_statement.body: For each source-admissible order $n$, let $\mathcal R_n$ be the binary sequences of period $2^n-1$ having exactly the run distribution of an order-$n$ binary $m$-sequence. Determine and prove an exact formula for the number of orbits of $\mathcal R_n$ under the group generated by cyclic rotation and sequence reversal.

scope.domain: Binary pseudorandom run sequences and their rotation-reversal equivalence classes
assumptions: Every sequence has the binary $m$-sequence run distribution
Equivalence is generated jointly by cyclic rotation and reversal
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source counts cyclic classes only. No inspected later result gives the exact number of joint rotation-reversal orbits for every admissible order.

citations.label: Kim--Song, run-sequence enumeration and distribution problems

progress.summary: The conclusion separately poses enumeration of binary run sequences under both rotation and reversal as a future research problem.
